title: Sydney Airport curfew and movement cap
summary: Sydney Airport, the busiest in Australia, has a curfew from 11 pm to 6 am under the Sydney Airport Curfew Act 1995 and a cap of 80 aircraft movements an hour under the Sydney Airport Demand Management Act 1997. Take-off and landing slots are scarce at peak times, and airlines that use their slots keep them from season to season (the slot rules were reformed from 2025; see the related reform).

instruments.title: Sydney Airport Demand Management Act 1997
instruments.provisions: movement cap of 80 an hour; slot management

direction_rationale: The cap and curfew limit the slots at the airport most airlines need, and slots held by incumbents are hard for new entrants to get, which limits competition on routes to and from Sydney.

assessment.summary: The curfew and the hourly cap limit how many flights can use Sydney Airport, so peak slots are scarce and mostly held by incumbents. New airlines struggle to get them.

marks.reason: Scarce peak slots, kept by the airlines that use them, make entry to Sydney routes harder.
